summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of gastroparesis, type 2 diabetes, and chronic abdominal pain was admitted for acute nausea, vomiting, and abdominal pain. She had not tolerated oral intake and presented with hyperglycemia and mild acute kidney injury likely due to dehydration. Supportive care with IV fluids, insulin, and antiemetics led to symptom improvement. Her potassium was mildly elevated, so lisinopril was held. A migraine developed during admission and responded to sumatriptan, with instructions to avoid concurrent tramadol due to serotonin syndrome risk. She advanced to a regular diet, remained stable, and was discharged home with follow-up planned with her primary care provider within 48 hours for medication review and diabetes management.
problems: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic autonomic (poly)neuropathy
Major depressive disorder, single episode, unspecified
Migraine, unspecified, not intractable, without status migrainosus
Elevated white blood cell count, unspecified
